text: air-work to air (dispatcher), on TP-479a Task 0-A, ahead of the Wave B decision; Wave A proceeds either way. 1) The exit as written cannot fail. The pack's figures: 11 blocks over 8 conflicted catch-ups (probes _count 6, probes entries 4, ledger rows 1). The 5 non-_count blocks sit in at most 5 catch-ups, so at least 3 of the 8 are _count-only whatever the per-PR split shows: the exit (3 or more ends the pack after Wave A) is decided by arithmetic before the measurement runs. 2) The exit compares a 13-merge count with the parent's 30-merge line (TP-479 line 510: 5 or fewer of 30). 5 leftover conflicted catch-ups per 13 merges projects to about 11.5 per 30, double the line. Rate-scaled, the leftover must be 2 or fewer at 13 (5 x 13/30 = 2.2), i.e. 6 or more of the 8 _count-only; the figures allow 3 to 6, so that threshold discriminates. Status: the arithmetic is verified against the pack's own numbers; that the census's blocks partition cleanly by catch-up is probable, unverified until --per-pr prints. Ask: the operator's ruling on which threshold 0-A reports against (as written, rate-scaled, or another). Meanwhile I build --per-pr, report the 8 catch-ups under both thresholds, and build Wave A; Wave B is not started before the ruling. lane/probes-count-derived starts now.

air-work to air (dispatcher), the data for request f5ec06 (TP-479a 0-A threshold). Measured 2026-10-12 by two oracles that agree. (1) The census's own replay, per catch-up, over the authoring window #180-#192: 12 catch-ups, 8 conflicted, the same 11 blocks the pack quotes (reproduced exactly). _count-only: #180, #184, #182 (one of its four), #192 = 4 of 8. Still conflicting without _count: #187 (entries), #188 (entries + one ledger member-row block), #186 (entries), #191 (entries) = 4. (2) The counterfactual itself: each conflicted probes file re-merged with git merge-file after stripping the _count line from base and both parents: the same 4 clean, the same 4 with one entries conflict each (two lanes appending at the roster's end). Read against the thresholds: as written (3 or more of 8) the pack ends after Wave A; rate-scaled (6 or more, since 4 leftovers per 13 merges projects to about 9.2 per 30 against the line's 5) Wave B is built. Outside the window: #177 (merged after #179) had 2 conflicted catch-ups on scripts/derived_population_census.py and ESPALIER_MEMORY.md, the parent's decision 2(a) record (DEF-4010), not this pack's. Wave A goes ahead either way; the pack's 0-A text now records the question as open. Also: the pack-artifact review returned REQUEST CHANGES (one BLOCK: Wave A named check_handoff_landing's _count, which is cc/GOAL_OWED.json's); the operator had me correct the pack on this lane and chose the hand-edit witness's home (check_ledger_probes prints a note naming live rows with no roster entry, never a refusal). The correction rides Wave A's PR.

air-work to air (dispatcher), for the seats whose lanes were branched before lane/probes-count-derived (PR #195): once it merges, task-packs/LEDGER_PROBES.json stores no _count. A lane on older code writes it back: its ledger verbs re-derive it, and its own ship.py catch-up runs the lane's record_merge.py, whose settle step reads the missing key as drift; GitHub then merges the lane with no settle step. The new tests/test_forward_ledger_completeness.py::test_the_live_roster_stores_no_total reds such a lane's CI after its catch-up and names the repair, from the repository root: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'tools/cc'); import record_merge as rm, generate_ledger_regions as g; from pathlib import Path; print(rm.settle_probes_count(Path('.'), g)[1])" then commit the probes file (driven 2026-10-12: one line dropped, nothing else moved). Lanes it can reach: any branched before #195 whose ship.py open or catch-up merges main in locally (the conflict path: its old settle step re-adds the key after ANY merge, even on a lane that never touched the ledger), and any whose own old verbs write the roster after that merge; today win's lane/audience-gate and lane/speedbump-margin-control, win-2's lane/merge-gate-proves-its-claims and lane/sandbox-posture. A server-side update-branch adds nothing. Also changed: check_ledger_probes.py no longer refuses on a count mismatch and prints a NOTE naming any live ledger id with no roster entry; ledger_row.py --reconcile-count is accepted and does nothing.
